title: Infra GPU fleet capacity, cloud-accounts, networking, IaC & CI/CD runbook
author: Aisha Khan
content:
Summary:
This document is the canonical team-wiki entry for managing Redwood's GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts and networking patterns, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD build pipelines that provision fleet resources. It consolidates capacity targets, autoscaling rules, ownership, runbook procedures, and Terraform module usage for day-to-day operations and incident response.

Scope:
- Applies to all production and staging GPU pools used by Redwood Dedicated and Hosted inference: gpu-pool-prod-*, gpu-pool-stage-*, and customer-dedicated-* clusters.
- Covers cloud account structure (AWS orgs and subaccounts), VPC networking, Transit Gateway patterns, IaC modules and CI/CD jobs that manage fleet lifecycle.
- Excludes low-level device drivers and vendor-specific BIOS tuning (handled by infra-hardware team).

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: Infra / GPU Fleet team (oncall alias: infra-gpu-oncall@redwood.internal).
- Secondary owner (networking & accounts): Cloud Networking team (oncall: cloud-net-oncall@redwood.internal).
- Pager escalation: 15m -> infra-gpu oncall; 30m -> infra lead; 60m -> eng-sre director.

Architecture overview (high level):
- Service names: fleet-manager (k8s operator), batch-provisioner, capacity-router, telemetry-agent (node exporter + custom GPU exporter).
- Pools: Each pool is a k8s nodegroup + daemonset for telemetry and nvpeer. Pools are tagged with : purpose, region, instance-type, capacity-class.
- Naming convention: gpu-pool-<env>-<region>-<instanceclass>-v<major>. Example: gpu-pool-prod-usw2-g5-1.

Capacity targets and SLOs:
- Target median GPU utilization per pool (steady-state): 40-60% (to maintain headroom for spikes).
- Scale-up threshold (alerting): sustained 75% avg GPU utilization for 10 minutes across pool -> evaluate for scale event.
- Critical threshold (incident): sustained >= 90% avg GPU utilization for 5 minutes OR queue length > 250 pending jobs -> trigger P1.
- Preemption SLA: nodes preempted more than 2% within 1h in a pool -> escalate to infra lead.
- Capacity buffer policy: maintain minimum 10% reserved capacity per pool for burst/latency-sensitive requests.

Monitoring and alerts (config snippets):
- Metrics ingested: gpu_utilization_percent, gpu_memory_used_mb, pending_requests, avg_latency_ms, node_ready_count.
- Example alert (Prometheus expression):
  - name: GPUHighUtilization
    expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent{pool=~"gpu-pool-prod-.*"}[10m]) > 75
    for: 10m
    severity: page

- Alert routing: GPUHighUtilization -> infra-gpu-oncall Slack channel + PagerDuty. Include runbook link.

Autoscaling and capacity management:
- Autoscaler types used:
  1) K8s Cluster Autoscaler (for nodegroup scaling).
  2) Fleet-level horizontal instance provisioning via batch-provisioner (Terraform-driven).
- Autoscaling policy summary:
  - Scale-up: trigger when average GPU utilization > 70% AND pending_requests > 50 for 5m. Provision min(20% of current nodes, 8 nodes) with instance class matching pool.
  - Scale-down: only after 30m of sustained utilization < 30% and node idle time > 40m; respect minimum node counts in config.
- Warm pools: Maintain warm nodes in each region for <100ms cold-start latency targets for latency-sensitive customers.

Cloud accounts and networking patterns:
- AWS account layout: org-root -> shared-services -> infra-prod -> infra-stage -> customer-dedicated-<id>. Each infra account has centralized logging and security guardrails (SCPs).
- VPC design:
  - Shared Transit Gateway for region connectivity. Use per-account VPCs with standardized subnet CIDR allocation table (see table below).
  - Public subnets: bastion, vpn-connector. Private subnets: worker nodes, telemetry, control-plane endpoints.
  - Egress: NAT Gateways in each AZ; prefer prefix-lists for security groups.

CIDR allocation (standardized):
| Account type | VPC CIDR range (example) | AZ subnets | Notes |
|-------------|--------------------------|-----------|-------|
| infra-prod  | 10.10.0.0/16             | 10.10.1.0/24 (AZ-a) etc. | reserved for system services |
| infra-stage | 10.11.0.0/16             | 10.11.1.0/24 ... | can overlap with dev but not prod |
| customer-dedicated-# | 10.20.#.0/22    | 3 AZ subnets | unique per customer account |

Security and network controls:
- All worker nodes enforce private-only egress for model artifacts; restricted service endpoints via VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, SSM).
- IAM roles: Use short-lived instance profiles from the token service and strict least-privilege policies for fleet-manager.
- KMS: all GCE/TLS artifacts must be encrypted with KMS keys scoped per-account.

IaC modules and structure (Terraform):
- Repo layout: infra-terraform/
  - modules/
    - gpu-nodegroup (manages launch templates, instance profiles, autoscaling groups)
    - k8s-addons (calico, metrics, fleet-manager helm chart)
    - vpc-standard (VPC, subnets, route tables, nat-gw)
    - transit-gw (TransitGateway attachments and route propagation)
  - envs/
    - prod/
    - stage/
- Module usage example (HCL snippet):
  module "gpu_nodegroup_usw2_g5" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra-terraform.git//modules/gpu-nodegroup"
    env = "prod"
    region = "us-west-2"
    instance_type = "g5.2xlarge"
    min_size = 4
    max_size = 256
    tags = { team = "infra" purpose = "inference" }
  }
- Terraform workspace pattern: <env>-<region>-<pool>. Example: prod-usw2-g5. Workspaces are required for state separation.
- State backend: remote S3 with locking via DynamoDB. Use per-account S3 bucket naming convention: redwood-terraform-state-<account>-<region>.

CI/CD pipelines (build and deploy):
- Repo CI jobs (CircleCI / GitHub Actions hybrid):
  - jobs/build-modules: lint, fmt, unit-validate (terraform validate + tflint).
  - jobs/plan-and-apply: Run terraform plan in PR, requires approvals from module owners. Apply done via gated pipeline controlled by a dedicated service account (ci-deployer).
  - jobs/helm-deploy-fleet: build and push helm chart to internal registry, then deploy to k8s via bot account.
- Gated deploy policy: Any terraform change to gpu-nodegroup or vpc-standard must be approved by at least two reviewers including infra-sre.
- Canary rollout steps for nodegroup changes:
  1. Create a canary nodegroup (gpu-pool-canary-<region>-<change-id>).
  2. Drain a small percentage of traffic to the canary (via capacity-router tag weights).
  3. Observe metrics for 30 minutes: gpu_utilization, error_rate, tail_latency.
  4. Promote or rollback via terraform workspace switch and apply.

Runbooks (operational playbook):
- P1: Pool at critical threshold (>=90% util OR queue > 250)
  1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and open incident in Incident Manager.
  2. Check telemetry dashboard: pool-by-pod, node counts, pending job queue.
  3. If autoscaler not triggered: manually scale nodegroup by +20% (terraform apply using emergency workspace) or trigger batch-provisioner to request additional instances.
  4. If network or control-plane issues: route to cloud-net-oncall.
  5. Notify customer success for any impacted customer-dedicated pools.
  6. Post-incident: run capacity triage and create follow-up ticket (owner: infra-gpu).

- P2: Gradual utilization increase (75% sustained for 10m)
  1. Review pending queues and identify noisy customers (use tagging + request metadata).
  2. Throttle non-critical background workloads using rate-limiter service (rl-service).
  3. Consider temporary upscaling of warm pool or adding burst instances.

- Node replacement / rolling upgrade steps:
  1. Create target nodegroup with new launch template.
  2. Add nodegroup to cluster, cordon and drain older nodes gradually (max 10% concurrently).
  3. Validate telemetry and pod readiness before deleting old nodes.

Testing and validation:
- Local Terraform testing: use terratest for module unit tests; run in ephemeral AWS account.
- Integration tests: provision a small canary pool in stage account and run the perf-suite (see /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
- CI gating: all plan diffs must include cost estimate (cost-estimator job) and potential impact on minimum node counts.

Common CLI ops and shortcuts:
- List pools: ./tools/fleetctl list-pools --env prod --region usw2
- Trigger emergency scale (authorized): ./tools/fleetctl scale --pool gpu-pool-prod-usw2-g5 --delta +16 --reason "P1 emergency"
- Terraform apply (approved flow): gh workflow run infra-apply.yml -f workspace=prod-usw2-g5 -f plan_id=<plan-id>

Audit and compliance considerations:
- All Terraform applies to prod must use signed commits and include linked change request in the PR description. CI logs and state access are audited via centralized logging.
- Sensitive customer VPC configs are labeled confidentiality:restricted in their workspace metadata.

Post-incident analysis and capacity planning cadence:
- Weekly capacity sync: infra-gpu + infra-sre + product capacity owner. Review 7-day utilization, trendline, and predicted 30-day needs.
- Quarterly model growth planning: finance + infra present forecast and required reserved instance commitments or cloud credits.

Appendix: quick reference table
| Item | Default value / command | Owner | Notes |
|------|-------------------------|-------|-------|
| Minimum warm nodes per region | 8 | infra-gpu | Adjust per customer SLA |
| Default instance class | g5.2xlarge | infra-gpu | change via module var instance_type |
| Terraform workspace name pattern | <env>-<region>-<pool> | infra-gpu | required |
| CI job for module lint | jobs/build-modules | infra-ci | runs on PR |

References and related pages:

- gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026 (operational runbook)
